chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Wuheyb ibn Hafs, from Abu Baseer who said:
I asked him (peace be upon him) about a snake that entered a container of water and exited from it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If you can find water other than it, so spill it.'

key_terms.لْيُهَرِقْهُ: let him pour it out/spill it

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on water contaminated by a snake entering and exiting it?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Abu Basir asks Imam al-Sadiq (AS) about the ruling of a snake entering a water container (*hubb*), to which the Imam replies that if other water is available, the contaminated water should be poured out. This reflects the principle of *kurr* water or general water purity in Shia fiqh, where the presence of a creature may render the water impure (*najis*) or require its disposal to ensure ritual validity, emphasizing practical ease when alternative water sources exist. The ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on removing doubt (*shubha*) in matters of purity through tangible action rather than complex calculation.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Wuheyb Bin Hafs, from Abu Baseer who said,
‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a snake which enters into a container of water and exits from it. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If you can find water other than it, so spill it’.
en.sarwar: 15. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Wuhayb ibn Hafs from abu Basir who has said the following:

“I once asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a snake that enters in a Hub (large water container) which has water in it and then comes out. He (the Imam) said, ‘If one can find other water it should be spilled away.’”
